chunks: From him, from al-Qasim, from Rifah, who said:

I asked him about the earnings of the cupper, so he said: 'Indeed, a man from the Ansar had a slave who was a cupper. He asked the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and he said to him: Do you have a draft animal? He said: Yes. He said: Then feed your draft animal.'

key_terms.نَاضِح: Draft animal (e.g., ox, donkey) used for work

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on the earnings of a cupper according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the permissibility of cupping (*hijama*) as a legitimate profession by citing a precedent where the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) instructed a cupper to feed his draft animal, thereby validating his earnings. In Shia jurisprudence, this serves as a foundational proof that income derived from medical services is lawful (*halal*) and sufficient for sustaining one's livelihood and tools of trade, countering earlier debates on the purity of such earnings.
